question.prompt: The largest integer \(n\) for which \(n^{200}\lt5^{300}\) is

solutions.explanation:
Rewrite both sides as hundredth powers to remove the large exponents:
\[
n^{200}=(n^2)^{100},\qquad 5^{300}=(5^3)^{100}=125^{100}.
\]
For nonnegative bases, taking the same positive integer power preserves their order. Since \(n^2\ge0\), the original inequality is therefore equivalent to
\[
n^2<125,\qquad\text{or}\qquad |n|<\sqrt{125}.
\]
Now \(11^2=121<125<144=12^2\), so \(11<\sqrt{125}<12\). Thus the allowed integers are \(-11,-10,\ldots,11\), and the largest is \(\boxed{11}\), choice D.
solutions.title: Reduce the large powers
